## Observed CI failure, not a deterministic runtime regression [PR #151](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/pull/151), head `98dec7bb04006660b1f606069505b3655260f607`, currently has a failed [Bun release (26) job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/42234284968/job/127947992636). The official checkout log identifies the tested synthetic merge as `552051b8404bb4fff81c11d3467ea1f074fdb8e9`, merging that head into `701aaca1a3b01d301b069ddd1b97baeb865aa13b`. This is not a default-branch release-job result. The full coverage suite reported **1,510 tests: 1,509 passed, 1 failed, zero canceled/skipped/todo**. The failure was: > two processes promote into one plain tracker without losing roots or corrupting shared artifacts At test/checkpoint-artifacts.test.ts:542 (assertion path :556), the test reported `Promoters exited before receipts: [[1,null],[0,null]]`. The failed child received SDK `lock_conflict` on `sdk-workspace-transaction`, reason `lock_owner_alive`, after **30,000 ms**, with zero owner handoffs. Test duration was about 34.55 seconds. The stack reaches commitPhaseDecision/index.ts:3288. The Bun gate invokes the Node coverage runner; the failed child identifies Node 26.13.0. ## Goal and expected versus actual behavior The [existing real-process regression](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/98dec7bb04006660b1f606069505b3655260f607/test/checkpoint-artifacts.test.ts#L542-L567) starts two promoters with `PM_LOCK_WAIT_MS=30000`, runs checkpoint collection, then requires both promotion receipts, both clean exits, retained promotion roots and an intact shared artifact. Expected for this positive concurrent-checkpoint fixture: complete both verified promotions and retain the shared artifact/root invariants within its declared bounds. Actual in this one hosted run: one child exhausted the bounded workspace lock wait, so the receipt/retention assertions were not reached and the release gate failed. The [existing bounded-contention contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/701aaca1a3b01d301b069ddd1b97baeb865aa13b/.agents/pm/features/pm-rl-qix7.toon) explicitly allows retryable lock_conflict after a bounded wait. **The refusal itself is not evidence of a broken lock contract.** Investigate the fixture's contention assumptions, lock duration and any justified bounded recovery before choosing a correction. ## Impact and limits - One observed hosted failure; no local reproduction or retry was performed. It does not establish a deterministic regression, a Bun runtime defect, a dependency regression, artifact corruption or data loss. - Node 22 and Node 26 npm release jobs in the same run passed. PR #151 changes release metadata, not this test or promotion implementation; no causal attribution to the version bump is made. - The printed coverage table is 100% lines/branches/functions, but this is a test failure, not a successful full gate. Subsequent identity audit, production audit, pack dry-run and changelog check were not reached in the failing job. Separate Bun graph-install verification was skipped. - This is distinct from [#140](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/issues/140), which owns stale workflow-approval wording at release-poll timeout. ## Acceptance / regression criteria 1. Reproduce or characterize the two-process checkpoint fixture under comparable full-gate instrumentation, recording lock wait/hold timing and owner lifecycle. Distinguish fixture scheduling assumptions from a product regression; retain an honest non-reproduction result if appropriate. 2. Preserve bounded lock semantics, promotion budgets, checkpoint integrity, both receipt/root assertions and collection safety. Do not silently accept a partial promotion, skip the test, weaken coverage thresholds, or simply relabel a failed full gate as passing. 3. If bounded retry/recovery is appropriate for the documented retryable contention outcome, prove it retains exactly-once effects and original durable identities, and cover exhaustion/fail-closed behavior. If a shorter critical section or fixture synchronization is needed, cover that behavior directly. 4. Verify the focused real-process regression and complete npm/Bun release gates on the eventual fix revision, with exact results and limits. ## Deduplication Checked all 151 all-status repository issues/PRs and 126 canonical tracker records at main `701aaca1`, plus current #151 discussion and related #92 discussion. No exact owner of this observed checkpoint-fixture failure was found. Closed checkpoint implementation [#92](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/pull/92) provides the positive scenario; existing pm-rl-bi4v and pm-rl-7c7m own different HTTP-crash-drill and packed-CLI timing cases. This issue is a narrow CI observation/investigation, not a request to relax the runtime's documented contention contract. --- ### GitHub comments (2) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-06T16:45:43Z) > > > > >

Drop into our [discord](https://discord.gg/coderabbit)! > **@unbraind** (2026-11-13T03:55:56Z) > > New hosted evidence for this existing checkpoint-fixture owner, after #158's 120-second admission change: > > On PR #153 head `d263ad1558c3d5905968fea254f0d45642539d10`, [Node22 job131635907428](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/43349219632/job/131635907428) reports **1686/1687 passed, one failure, zero cancelled/skipped**. The sole failure is `test/checkpoint-artifacts.test.ts:607`, “two processes promote into one plain tracker without losing roots or corrupting shared artifacts”, after about121.16 seconds: `Promoter exited before receipt`, followed by child `DOMException [TimeoutError]: The operation was aborted due to timeout`. Child runtime is Node22.23.4. The printed coverage table is100%, but the gate fails. > > This differs from the original30-second `lock_conflict/lock_owner_alive` evidence. Current `test/fixtures/checkpoint-promoter.ts` passes `AbortSignal.timeout(120_000)` to `environment.fit`; the parent sets `PM_LOCK_WAIT_MS=120000` and a900-second test limit. The log does not establish which internal operation exhausted the fit budget or whether contention, scheduling or another delay caused it. It is not evidence of lost roots, corrupt checkpoints or a new lock defect. The same-head [Node26](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/43349219632/job/131635907376) and [Bun26](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/43349219632/job/131635907040) checks are now successful. > > The canonical [pm-rl-0x9x item](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/d263ad1558c3d5905968fea254f0d45642539d10/.agents/pm/issues/pm-rl-0x9x.toon) remains in progress; retaining this new observation here avoids a duplicate issue. > > Validation needed: characterize fit-budget consumption and actual lock/progress phases under comparable instrumentation, then verify both original promotion receipts, clean exits, original durable identities, exactly-once charges, both ledger roots, matching verified checkpoints and one retained artifact. Preserve deliberate held-owner refusal controls and production lock safety; do not mark a partial promotion or a printed coverage percentage as a passing gate. Keep bounded non-reproduction results if the timeout cannot be reproduced. No independent local reproduction or root-cause diagnosis was performed in this review.
